Ophthalmology · published research

Orbital implant exposure

In one randomized comparison, conjunctival healing occurred in 97.1% of laser-treated patients and 74.3% of patients receiving drugs plus surgery. Healing was also faster in both severity strata.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

In one randomized comparison, conjunctival healing occurred in 97.1% of laser-treated patients and 74.3% of patients receiving drugs plus surgery. Healing was also faster in both severity strata.

Summary of the Evidence

Two publications are listed in the exact orbital-implant category. One is a randomized human comparison that also includes a rabbit experiment; the other is an in-vitro endothelial-cell study of angiogenesis. The human report concerns exposure of hydroxyapatite implants specifically, not all orbital implant complications. Xu et al. 2015

Human and clinical evidence

The randomized comparison included 70 patients with exposed hydroxyapatite orbital implants, 35 assigned to He-Ne laser and 35 to drugs plus surgery. Conjunctival wound-healing rates were 97.14% and 74.29%, respectively. In mild exposure, reported healing time was about 7.2 days with laser versus 14.3 days with the comparator. In moderate-to-severe exposure, it was about 18.2 versus 31.3 days. The report is one clinical publication from one research group; independent confirmation and contemporary replication are not listed.

Animal evidence

The same publication describes 24 New Zealand white rabbits with orbital implants. Tissue and imaging findings were interpreted as increased implant vascularization and reduced inflammation after treatment. These animal outcomes are part of the same publication and are not an independent clinical cohort.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

A separate cell study reports that low-level laser exposure changed endothelial-cell proliferation, migration, and lumen formation through a miRNA and VEGFA pathway. It is mechanistic work and does not measure conjunctival wound closure in patients.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The human protocol used 633 nm He-Ne exposure for 15 minutes daily over ten days. The rabbit experiment and endothelial-cell protocol are distinct. The clinical result applies to the studied implant material and exposure severity; parameters and surgical practice may differ in other settings.

Interpretation

The randomized comparison is a positive clinical signal, supported by a parallel animal experiment, but it is a single report. Further independent controlled studies are needed to confirm the healing advantage, evaluate complications, and establish whether the protocol applies to other orbital implants.

Evidence strength in source summaryConjunctival-wound healing: One randomized comparative signal Cellular angiogenesis: Laboratory only
Publications and records2 publications: 1 randomized human comparison with 70 patients and a parallel rabbit experiment involving 24 animals, plus 1 in-vitro endothelial-cell paper.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

One randomized clinical comparison of 70 patients reports higher healing and shorter healing times with He-Ne irradiation than drugs plus surgery, with a parallel rabbit experiment. A separate cell study is mechanistic. Clinical replication and generalizability beyond hydroxyapatite implant exposure are lacking.

Publication and study types

  • The human and rabbit arms are within one publication and are not separate publications.
  • No independent clinical replication or overlapping human cohort is listed.

Research countries listed

  • China
